sections.bio: I enjoy coding, math, chess, writing, and connecting with cool people. Send a connection request if that's you

posts.text:
"the linkedin algorithm is cooked"
"where is my reach"

Honestly, I'm still just amazed that I get a single like on my posts.

It's crazy to me that people can randomly post their random thoughts on a random day
And people around the world will see it and take time out of their day to engage with it.

My stats might not be considered great
But every time I get a single like,
That's my expectations being blown away.

Imagine you walk into a room full of people and just randomly start talking
And then the room goes quiet to listen
40 people clap
And 25 people come up to you afterwards to compliment you and tell them how much they loved your speech.

That would be pretty cool.

I don't take having an audience for granted.
It's still mind-blowing to me that 4600 people decided to hit the follow button on my profile.

And even after I haven't made a real post in like a month
There are still people listening?!

Genuinely, thank you.

And if you want to build an audience of your own
It's literally as simple as hitting post
Engaging with others
And expecting nothing in return.

If you ever want any help, slide into my DMs.

It's crazy that this platform exists.

We're now two-thirds through 2026.

Are you satisfied with how it's going so far?

To be honest, I'm not.

A lot of great things have happened.
I feel like I grew as a person.

But all the same
It feels like there's a clock constantly ticking down inside of me.

There's only so much time left in high school or even my teenage years
And so many things I haven't yet crossed off my bucket list.

These are the days that I'll look back on with a smile once I'm older
And I want to make the most of them.

There have been too many empty promises
Too many relapses into bad habits
Too many wasted hours.

But there's still 4 months to change the tone of the entire year.

If we lock in and put the right systems in place
Then in December
We'll all be dancing like these cows
Instead of sitting sadly like potatoes.

WE GOT THIS.

I have a couple of things planned.

I'll be dropping some things
Starting some things
And posting here and there with updates on how it's going.

Stay tuned.

How are you feeling about 2026 so far?

Small-group mentorship with YC founders, F500 executives, multi-millionaires, and more

Structured curriculum tracks designed to help you develop real-world skills relevant to your career

A community of ambitious, like-minded students that you match with to build startups with 

All for FREE.
But only for a limited number of spots.

Sai, Dhairya, Mahathi, Harish, Kejun, and I are building something huge.

Our leader and mentor, Joshua Newall,
Has advised Fortune 500 companies at scale,
Chats with YC founders for fun,
And is the kind of guy who you could talk with for hours and never run out of stories.

Together, we’ve designed a program that teaches you everything school forgot.

It’s a long-term commitment.
Even after the curriculum concludes,
The exclusive community and opportunities last forever.

Our free founding cohort runs from September 1st - 30th
And we’re only taking 30-50 people.

Want to apply?

Fill out the quick 10-minute application on our website here: https://high-agency.io

First 10 applications receive priority consideration.
After that, refer your friends and/or use a referral code from a friend to get priority.

But the thing we care about most
Is your high agency.

It doesn’t matter how good your grammar is or 
Or how many buzzwords you include
As long as you show that you have an inner drive to lead your own unique life.

So just be yourself.
And show us why you are amazing.

If you want my referral link,
Comment “AGENCY” and why you think you should get it!

I’ll DM you if you’re a good fit.

Deadline is August 25.

Best of luck!

Almost a year ago,
I received a random LinkedIn DM that changed everything.

It was from a complete stranger
Who simply told me that he was building a program
Designed to help students to develop “high agency.”

“What even is that?” I thought to myself.

So I searched it up.
Gemini told me it was
“having the strong power and clear ability to take charge of your own life.”

That’s the one thing that’s missing from most people these days.

We all have a victim mindset.

“It’s impossible to find a j*b…”
“Only legacy students get accepted to top colleges…”
“AI is going to take over…”

Sure, some of those statements might be partially true.
And it sucks.

But most people simply ride with the flow of life
Let the systems and current events dictate them.

High agency is the determination to create your own opportunities.
Lead the life YOU want.
No matter what hidden rules or norms are present in modern society.

When I joined this program
I was placed into a cohort with 5 other people.

And I was taken aback.

They moved at the speed of light.
No hesitation. No waiting.

Sai Amartya Balamurugan Lakshmipraba built a Telegram integration for Aside (YC F25) and secured a paid remote internship that didn’t initially exist.

Mahathi Dharmavaram developed a real-world implementation of Rocket League using Arduino-powered RC vehicles.

Dhairya Shah published a mobile app to the Google Play store and got 200k+ views from social media.

Kejun (Renée) L. has volunteered over 235 hours running craft stations, game booths, beach cleanups, and community events across Irvine.

Harish Ramasubramanian built an app and scaled it to 50,000+ active users within months with minimal marketing.

They’re all breaking through the limits of what high schoolers are “supposed” to do.

And together, we’re building a program to help you join us.

More details coming soon.

I went in as #20
Came out as #2.

This past week, I played in the WIM Ruth Haring Tournament of Girls State Champions
An invitation-based tournament that pooled the top scholastic girl from each of the 50 US states into a single event.

My whole family piled into a car and drove 12 hours to the venue in Michigan
And I missed the first two days of school to compete.

I didn't have any expectations going in
Especially since I was almost in the bottom half of the players in terms of rating
But I ended up winning 2nd place with a score of 4.5/6
Earning a $280 cash prize and $4,000 university scholarship + $100 best game award!

But it wasn't just about the chess.

I also reunited with my amazing chess friends
Who I've kept in touch with but hadn't seen in over a year at this point.

We went to events together
Strolled randomly around town
And ate meals together.

We also made a pact that we would get ice cream on the last day
And whoever placed the highest would have to pay.

Totally worth the $50.

There's something special about a tournament of only girls.

Everyone is friendly.
Everyone gives each other gifts.
And every round is insanely unpredictable
Because girls generally play in fewer tournaments so their skill level sometimes doesn't match their published rating.

It's not an experience I'll forget anytime soon.

Now it's back home and back to school 😭
